restrictions: The two messages have 23 and 24 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 1 prefix round, standard IV and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.
Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word; the output is a collision for every value of this coin, so there is no failed trial and no restart.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; a program with no loop, no restart and no branch before the final collision check (step 4 of the proof, which has one comparison and one conditional branch, both charged), with memory traffic charged at four primitive operations per data operation, and a final verification by two complete hash evaluations included.
No preprocessing, table, stored collision or nonuniform advice; the preprocessing and advice fields are zero-valued upper bounds because the schema cannot express log2(0).

Specific to the 1-round prefix: the identity is proved for one round only, nothing is claimed for two or more rounds (the witness pair has different digests there), and no priority or novelty claim is made.
